newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-DEFENDING CHAMPION BECKER OPENS WITH WORKMANLIKE WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DEFENDING CHAMPION BECKER OPENS WITH WORKMANLIKE WIN.

text.p: Defending champion Boris Becker opened his campaign at the ATP world tennis championship with a workmanlike 6-4 7-5 victory over Russia's French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov on Tuesday.

Roared on by a fanatical 12,000 German crowd who cheered and stamped their feet every time he hit a winning shot, Becker used his strong serve-and-volley game to clinch the round-robin red group match in just 78 minutes.
Becker, who turns 29 later this week, has been playing some brilliant tennis in the last month after bouncing back to his best following a serious wrist injury at Wimbledon.

But the German has been drawn in the toughest group of the round-robin stage with world number one Pete Sampras and his American rival Andre Agassi. It was important for Becker to get off to a solid start against Kafelnikov.
After both players struggled to hold their serve in the opening few games, Becker made a key break of serve in the fifth game on his way to the first set.

The second set was tight until Becker broke again to lead 6-5 after Kafelnikov hit a forehand out of court. Becker, who struck a total of 17 aces in the match, then served out for the match in the next game.

The championship, which brings together the top eight players in the world, is played in a round-robin format in the early stages. The top two players from each of two groups advance to the semifinals.

Dutchman Richard Krajicek, who has struggled with motivation problems since his Wimbledon triumph this year, was firing on all cylinders in a 6-4 6-4 victory over Michael Chang in the opening match of the white group.
Krajicek took 62 minutes to defeat the American world number two in a white group match, hitting 20 aces in the process.
It was a confidence-boosting performance from the towering Dutchman who just managed to qualify for the season-ending tournament as the eighth player in the world rankings.
"That was my best performance against a big player since Wimbledon," Krajicek said. "I was very happy with my game, especially my strengths -- my forehand and serve."

Wimbledon marked Krajicek's only tournament victory this year. Having clinched the first grand slam title of his career, the towering Dutchman admits he has struggled to lift himself mentally for other events.
Chang was playing a highly-motivated Krajicek, however.
"Richard really served very well," Chang said. "Richard has come here with nothing to lose. He was the last guy in...that showed in the way he played."
